title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CARLA'S CEILING
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Carla Benson, a 911 dispatcher in Albuquerque, New Mexico.
All night, she stays calm while the whole city panics.
Then, at six every morning, a trumpet blasts through her ceiling.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BROOM
segments.quote: Whatever is begun in anger ends in shame.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: On the third morning, Carla grabbed a broom to bang on the ceiling.
Then she saw her grandpa's old fridge magnet, from Benjamin Franklin:
Whatever is begun in anger ends in shame.
She put the broom down. She went to bed angry, and woke up only grumpy. Progress.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE KNOCK
segments.quote: Everything that irritates us about others can lead us to an understanding of ourselves.
segments.author: Carl Jung
lines: That afternoon she knocked upstairs. Mister Teo Ortiz, seventy-eight, opened the door.
I play at six, he said. Always have. I don't change my ways.
Carla thought of her own strict schedule and rules. She remembered the Swiss doctor Carl Jung:
Everything that irritates us about others can lead us to an understanding of ourselves.
He was stubborn. So was she. So she asked, why six?

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE SONG
segments.quote: When it sounds good, it is good.
segments.author: Duke Ellington
lines: His wife Rosa, seventy-six, still leaves for her bakery shift at six.
For fifty-one years, he has played her out the door.
Teo shrugged and quoted his hero, Duke Ellington:
When it sounds good, it is good.
The next morning, Carla listened. It sounded good. So he moved to the front window, and she bought earplugs.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SILENCE
segments.quote: Act as if what you do makes a difference. It does.
segments.author: William James
lines: One Tuesday, no trumpet. The quiet woke her up.
Not my business, she thought. Then she remembered the American thinker William James:
Act as if what you do makes a difference. It does.
She knocked. Teo had a fever and a bad cough, and Rosa was at work.
Carla called his doctor, then brought him a pot of green chile stew.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LONG NIGHT
segments.quote: Friendship adds a brighter radiance to prosperity and lessens the burden of adversity by dividing and sharing it.
segments.author: Cicero
lines: A week later, Carla worked all night on a lost hiker. Found safe at dawn, but she was wiped out.
On the stairs, Teo handed her coffee and quoted Cicero, the old Roman:
Friendship adds a brighter radiance to prosperity and lessens the burden of adversity by dividing and sharing it.
So she told him all about it. Her shoulders came down for the first time in years.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE LESSON
segments.quote: Life is long if you know how to use it.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: Carla said, I always wanted to play trumpet, but I'm thirty-four. Too late.
Teo laughed. You sound like me before Rosa. Then he quoted Seneca, the Roman thinker:
Life is long if you know how to use it.
Now, every Saturday, she plays a little. The neighbors call it the goose song. She plays it anyway.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Wait out anger. Look inward. Listen. Show up. Share the load. Start now.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Wait out the anger. Look at yourself. Listen to the song. Show up. Share the load. Start now.
I tried the trumpet once. My cat moved out.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
